assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is a central problem of biological energy conversion and catalysis: how a metalloenzyme couples ATP-driven electron transfer to the reduction of N2. Crystal structures of the MoFe protein and FeMo cofactor, including the interstitial carbide, together with kinetic mechanism work, have defined the field in physical, mechanistic terms. This is the type of structure plus kinetics achievement I value most.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle are the clearest structural contributors (MoFe protein, cofactor composition and carbide). Seefeldt and Dean built the kinetic and genetic framework; Ribbe also contributed. Three slots cannot cover everyone, so I would weigh structure versus mechanism and expert-report evidence.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent structural, spectroscopic and kinetic work; the field is mature. The catalytic cycle, particularly the substrate-binding state of the cofactor, is still debated, but the structural discovery itself is stable and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: How to apportion credit between structural and mechanistic/genetic contributors, and whether Dean and Ribbe are excluded unfairly.
Whether the unresolved turnover mechanism weakens the case for a mechanism-based prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins established, with quantitative distance and driving-force dependences, how redox cofactors communicate across proteins. It is a physical-mechanism result with kinetics directly relevant to respiratory enzymes. Marcus theory was already honored, so this candidacy rests on the experimental biological realization.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler form a compact and clean pairing, with the Ru-modified protein experiments and tunneling-pathway analyses. Related contributors (Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton, Moser) are not in the supplied credit, which raises a priority question I would need to examine.
assessment.maturity: The results are decades old, widely confirmed and part of textbook bioenergetics, so timeliness is good if anything late.
uncertainties: Whether the contribution is a line of work rather than a single sharply attributable discovery.
Overlap with Marcus's prize and the role of Dutton and Moser-type work not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a transformative synthetic method, used daily in pharmaceutical and materials chemistry, building on earlier cross-coupling recognition with a distinct bond-forming capability and clear mechanistic understanding.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the ligand-enabled general reaction independently and are the natural pair. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a precursor, not the general method, though a priority question remains.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with large independent adoption and a stable interpretation. The 2010 prize on cross-coupling slightly lowers novelty, but not the substance.
uncertainties: Whether the 2010 cross-coupling prize makes this appear incremental to some members.
Priority treatment of Kosugi and Migita precursors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert bases at target loci without double-strand breaks, a conceptual advance in chemistry applied to genome editing with rapid therapeutic impact. Chemical design of the deaminase fusions is original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the work, with Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors, including evolved deaminase) as lead inventors. Kondo and Nishida pursued a related Target-AID approach. The credit can fit a fair configuration, but the third laureate slot is contestable and CRISPR was honored in 2020.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation and clinical entry, though long-term clinical outcomes are still unfolding. Timeliness is plausible but could be considered slightly early.
uncertainties: Whether the Nobel Prize in 2020 for CRISPR makes this a follow-on rather than a stand-alone discovery.
Treatment of Kondo and Nishida's parallel work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structures of radiation-sensitive and microcrystalline samples and time-resolved structural movies of reactions. It makes mechanisms visible in the way I value, including photosystem and light-driven proteins.
assessment.attribution: Chapman, Fromme and Hajdu are plausible principal contributors (the 2011 photosystem I demonstration, diffract-before-destroy concept). Schlichting and others, plus Spence, Neutze and the facility builders, complicate the three-laureate limit and priority.
assessment.maturity: The method is confirmed at several facilities and used widely, although the number of fully resolved mechanistic breakthroughs is still limited. Some physics-oriented parts may belong elsewhere.
uncertainties: Chemistry versus physics balance and the role of the facility builders and the Spence and Neutze group.
Whether the mechanistic payoff is mature enough compared to the technical advance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing transformed biology and medicine, with sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry (reversible terminators, fluorescent readout) at its core. The impact is enormous and the chemistry is concrete.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented Solexa chemistry; Rothberg commercialized pyrosequencing-based 454, which was a distinct line. Mayer and Ju contributed other approaches. Credit is spread across competing technologies, so a fair three-person split is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and with unmatched impact, though the delay in recognition has not removed the priority tension.
uncertainties: Whether the work is more a technology and company development than a clean chemical discovery.
Which of the competing sequencing chemistries should be recognized.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates through liquid-liquid phase separation reframed intracellular organization with physical-chemistry concepts. The intellectual impact is large and the physical language fits my own preference for principle-based explanations.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne published the founding P-granule result; Rosen contributed in vitro multivalent-interaction frameworks. Pappu and Mittag are also important, so the allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: The field is young and still debates mechanism, in-cell relevance and artifacts, so the maturity case is weaker than for other candidates.
uncertainties: Rigor of in vivo evidence for phase separation as opposed to other assemblies.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is the physical basis of many respiratory and photosynthetic reactions, so a mechanistic framework with theory and model systems is important. Its impact on catalysis such as water oxidation and fuel formation is clear.
assessment.attribution: Mayer (thermochemical and concerted PCET framework), Hammes-Schiffer (theory) and Nocera (model and catalysis) are plausible. Meyer is also credited and was an early pioneer. A compound discovery whose parts may need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally and theoretically well established, though the unifying body of work is diffuse and no single decisive event marks it.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution across theory, spectroscopy and catalysis.
Whether it rests on a line of work and not one clearly attributable discovery.
I have a personal field overlap and would recuse myself or seek external expert views.
